title: Reverse Part of a List
statement:
Reverse the nodes of a linked list from position `left` to position `right` (both counted from `1`, both included) and leave all other nodes where they are. Return the head of the list.

Do it by re-linking the existing nodes, in a single pass.

examples.explanation: The nodes at positions 2 to 4 (2, 3, 4) are reversed: 4, 3, 2.
Reversing a single node changes nothing.

hints.nudge: Only the part between the two positions changes. Which node must you hold on to so that the reversed part can be linked back in?
hints.pattern: A dummy node, a `prev` pointer standing just before position `left`, and repeated moving of the node after `cur` to the front of the reversed part.
hints.pseudocode:
dummy.next = head; prev = dummy
move prev forward left - 1 times
cur = prev.next
repeat right - left times:
  nxt = cur.next
  cur.next = nxt.next
  nxt.next = prev.next
  prev.next = nxt
return dummy.next
hints.walkthrough: Walk to the node `prev` right before the first node to reverse; a dummy node in front of the head makes this work even when left is 1. Let `cur` be the first node of the part (it will end up as its LAST node). Now take the node right after `cur` and move it to the front of the part (right after `prev`): cur.next skips it, it points to what was first, and prev.next points to it. Doing this right - left times turns the part around, and `cur` keeps pointing at the old first node, which stays in place while the others are inserted before it. No nodes are created, one pass, O(n) time and O(1) memory.
